access_note: Free download (the website asks for an account); vendor OS images are licensed separately.
description: GNS3 is a graphical network emulation platform that runs real network operating system images (for example router and switch images from Cisco, Juniper, Arista and open-source routers) in virtual machines, containers or emulators, links them in drag-and-drop topologies, and lets engineers configure and test them as if they were physical networks. It consists of a desktop GUI and a server that can run locally, in the GNS3 VM, or on remote hosts, and it is used for training, certification practice, design validation and troubleshooting. It is developed by GNS3 Technologies with a large community; the latest stable version in the repository tags is 3.0.6, with 3.1 in alpha. Coverage: user-built topologies limited by the host's computing resources, typically tens to a few hundred devices; no geographic data. Format and access: installers for Windows, macOS and Linux and Python source on GitHub; free of charge under the GNU GPL version 3, although vendor images must be obtained under their own licences. Caveats: performance scales with hardware and image weight; vendor images can be costly or restricted; it emulates control and data planes but not physical-layer impairments. Simulation uses: testing routing resilience and cascading failures of provider and exchange networks, capacity and configuration planning, and operator digital-twin labs. Related records: Mininet is a lighter Linux-based emulator, and ns-3 and OMNeT++ simulate, not emulate networks; CAIDA and PeeringDB data can inform topologies.
